summary: The principles for typed failures and cancellation are clear, but the operational-failure payloads and constructor set are underspecified; the biggest gap is the conflict with ADR 0017 over whether delivery outcomes are persisted.

questions.text: What are the shapes of StorageDiagnostic and ProcessDiagnostic, and which stable code and message does each OperationalFailure render as?
questions.reason: The CLI envelope needs diagnostic objects for exit 3; 0019 gives 'StorageUnavailable StorageDiagnostic | RuntimeUnavailable ProcessDiagnostic | CompilerUnavailable String | GitUnavailable String' with undefined payloads.

questions.text: ADR 0019 says ADR 0017 assigns persistent delivery/dispatch outcomes and restart behaviour to Delivery, but ADR 0017 rules out any delivery ledger, dispatch record or persistent receipt.
questions.reason: Decides whether a durable delivery store exists; 0019 'ADR 0017 assigns persistent delivery/dispatch outcomes to Delivery' vs 0017 'There is no mandatory delivery ledger, dispatch-intent record or delivery ID'.

questions.text: Which OperationalFailure constructor carries guest protocol violations, transport and provider failures and internal kernel defects, and is the set closed?
questions.reason: 0007 requires protocol failures to 'remain distinguishable' and 0006 names dhall.internal-* defects, but the four constructors have no obvious home for them.

questions.text: What mechanism reports progress of long operations to the owning caller across CLI, MCP and Web?
questions.reason: A progress effect would enter many operation rows; 0019 'Report progress and results to the owning caller' and 0025 'report that progress' name no mechanism.

questions.text: Can a single in-flight operation be cancelled within a long-lived MCP or Web server, or only by stopping the process?
questions.reason: Per-request cancellation needs per-request threads and an MCP cancellation handler; 0019 says 'Cancellation is operation-scoped' and 'exercised through the operation's owning caller/process'.

questions.text: Does any operation impose default deadlines or timeouts on guests, compilers, HTTP requests or model turns?
questions.reason: 0019 says deadline policy is 'separate from data contracts' and tuned 'from measurements', leaving whether defaults exist open.
